metaDescription: Six julienne peelers that cut thin vegetable strips for salads and slaws, compared by blade layout, handle comfort, cleanup and whether they also peel.
introParagraphs: A julienne peeler turns a carrot, zucchini or cucumber into thin, even matchsticks in a few strokes, with no mandoline, no knife skills and no big gadget to wash. Some models are strip-cutters only, and others pair a smooth peeling edge with a toothed julienne edge so a single tool covers both jobs. That choice, plus handle comfort and how easily food fibers rinse out of the teeth, decides which one fits your kitchen.

We evaluated six picks from the specifications and features shown on their product pages, covering blade layout, steel, handle shape, cleaning aids and safety covers. WorthRated is written for active adults who cook often and the family members who shop for them. Nothing here is a medical product, and no hands-on lab measurement was involved.

In short, the OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler is the dedicated strip cutter with a safety cover, the OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler is the compact Y option, and the Deiss PRO, Vibrant Kitchen, Deepfeel and Sunkuka are the peel-and-julienne combinations. The sections below sort out which suits your cooking.

products.name: OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler
products.description:
The OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler is a dedicated strip cutter, with a hardened stainless steel julienne blade rather than a combined peel-and-cut edge. The listing says it suits garnishes and zucchini, and it comes with a clear flip-top safety cover that protects the blade. A soft, comfortable, non-slip handle cushions the hand during repetitive strokes.

Because the blade only does one job, the teeth can be tuned for clean strips instead of compromising with a peeling edge. That is why it earns the lead spot for cooks who mostly want matchsticks. The tradeoff is that you will need a second tool for ordinary peeling, so it adds to your drawer instead of replacing something.

The flip-top cover is the standout ownership detail, since a toothed blade is not something you want loose against your fingers in a drawer. Compared with the OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler, this one is purely for strips and carries the cover, while the Prep model works as a compact Y shape. Against the Deiss PRO, it lacks a peel function but is simpler to use. It also makes a tidy gift for someone who loves salads but hates fiddly knife work.
products.bestFor: Cooks who mainly want clean matchsticks and a safety cover for the teeth.
pros: Dedicated julienne blade focuses on clean strips
Flip-top clear cover protects blade and fingers
Soft non-slip handle cushions repeated strokes
Hardened stainless steel blade
cons: Does not double as a regular peeler

products.name: OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler
products.description:
The OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler is a compact Y-shaped tool that cuts precise strips from carrots, cucumber, zucchini and more. The listing says the Y shape is easy to maneuver and works with every grip. Sharp, durable stainless steel blades will not rust, and the handle is non-slip and ergonomic.

A Y frame suits the pulling stroke that julienne cutting needs, because the blade sits across the top and you draw it toward you along the vegetable. The compact size keeps the tool light and easy to tuck away. The tradeoff is that it is a strips-first tool, so it is not meant to replace a general peeler for potatoes.

It is dishwasher safe, which is a real advantage given how food fibers can lodge in toothed blades. Compared with the OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler, it has a Y frame but the listing does not mention a safety cover. Next to the Sunkuka, it is simpler, with no extra cleaning brush or eye remover listed. Because it is compact, it is a sensible pick for small kitchens, dorm rooms and RVs.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a small Y-shaped julienne tool that goes in the dishwasher.
pros: Compact Y frame is easy to maneuver
Stainless steel blades resist rust
Non-slip ergonomic handle works with every grip
Dishwasher safe cleanup
cons: Not a replacement for a general peeler

products.name: Deiss PRO Dual Julienne Peeler and Vegetable Peeler
products.description:
The Deiss PRO Dual Julienne Peeler is a two-in-one tool that peels and cuts julienne strips, which the maker describes as replacing separate gadgets. Its stainless steel blades are said not to rust, and the non-slip handle is meant to give a firm grip. The listing mentions garnishes and zucchini noodles as ideas for everyday cooking.

Being able to switch between peeling and julienning saves reaching for a second tool, and the compact frame fits into a drawer or hangs from a loop. The tradeoff with any combination tool is that each function is a compromise: the peel side will not be as specialized as a dedicated swivel, and the julienne teeth will not rival a dedicated cutter.

It is dishwasher safe, and the lifetime warranty is the longest support promise in this lineup. Compared with the OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler, it covers more jobs but has no safety cover mentioned. Next to the Vibrant Kitchen, it is a similar two-in-one concept with a warranty attached. The hanging loop makes it easy to keep within reach near the stove.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a single tool that peels and julienne cuts, backed by a lifetime warranty.
pros: Peels and julienne cuts in one tool
Lifetime warranty
Hanging loop and compact frame
Dishwasher safe stainless steel

products.name: Vibrant Kitchen 2-in-1 Peeler and Julienne Shredder
products.description:
The Vibrant Kitchen tool pairs a straight peeling edge with a serrated julienne side on a dual-sided 420J2 stainless steel blade. The listing says the carrot shredder side makes fine strips and the cabbage shredder side turns a head into slaw. The ergonomic handle is 5.6 inches long and designed to hold firm in wet hands.

The extra cabbage shredding is what makes it different, since most julienne peelers focus only on carrots and zucchini. That versatility helps if you make coleslaw or stir-fry. The serrated side will not give the same clean cuts on soft produce as a dedicated julienne blade, and you must flip the tool to switch sides.

It rinses clean under water or in the dishwasher, and the maker pitches it as a way to replace a drawer of gadgets. Compared with the Deiss PRO, it adds the cabbage side and a stated handle length but has no warranty listed. Against the OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler, it covers more tasks but lacks the flip-top cover. It is a good fit for anyone who cooks a lot of stir-fries and salads.
products.bestFor: Cooks who make slaw and carrot strips and want one tool for peeling too.
pros: Handles carrots, zucchini and cabbage
Hardened 420J2 stainless edge resists rust
5.6-inch handle holds firm in wet hands
Rinses clean or goes in the dishwasher
cons: Serrated side is less precise on soft produce

products.name: Sunkuka 3-in-1 Y Julienne Peeler
products.description:
The Sunkuka is an all-metal Y-shaped peeler built from 18/8 stainless steel that peels, julienne cuts and removes potato eyes. The dual-blade system switches between smooth peeling and precision julienne slicing, and the listing mentions zoodles, veggie noodles and salads. The wide, balanced Y handle is designed for right and left hands.

The open-frame design rinses clean quickly, and the included cleaning brush helps clear food fibers from the julienne teeth, which is a thoughtful touch. The sturdy all-metal build resists bending, but metal handles offer less cushioning than the soft grips on the OXO models. The listing does not give dimensions or weight.

A hanging hole supports hook storage and it is dishwasher safe. Compared with the OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler, it adds a peeling edge and the brush but loses the soft handle. Next to the Deepfeel, it is all metal instead of plastic-handled, making it a sturdier but harder-feeling tool. Keep the brush handy, because julienne teeth are the part that gets dirty first.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a sturdy all-metal 3-in-1 tool with a cleaning brush.
pros: Peels, julienne cuts and removes eyes
Cleaning brush clears julienne teeth
18/8 stainless steel resists rust and bending
Hanging hole for storage

products.name: Deepfeel 2-in-1 Julienne and Vegetable Peeler
products.description:
The Deepfeel combines a smooth straight blade for everyday peeling with a julienne blade for thin, even strips. Two stainless steel blades pivot with curved surfaces for smooth peeling, according to the listing. A wide Y-shaped non-slip handle is meant to give balanced control for left and right hands and to reduce hand fatigue.

The swivel action is the difference from many combination tools, which use fixed blades. It makes the peeling side friendlier to round produce like potatoes and apples. The tradeoff is the same one all combos face: the julienne blade shares space with a peeling edge, so it is less specialized than a dedicated cutter.

It is built with a rust-resistant stainless steel body and is dishwasher safe. Compared with the Sunkuka, it offers swivel blades but no cleaning brush. Against the OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler, it adds a real peeling function at the cost of simplicity. The pivoting blades are a nice touch for people who peel round produce more than long carrots.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a swivel peeler that can also julienne.
pros: Swivel blades follow curved produce
Wide Y handle is non-slip and balanced
Straight and julienne blades in one tool
Dishwasher safe stainless construction

buyingCriteria.explanation: A dedicated cutter such as the OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler focuses on clean strips, while combination tools like the Deiss PRO and Deepfeel add a peeling edge. Combos save drawer space and money on gadgets. Dedicated cutters usually give tidier matchsticks and often carry a safety cover. Choose a dedicated tool if julienning is your goal, and a combo if you want fewer tools. If you already own a good swivel peeler, the dedicated route avoids duplicating a function you have.

The teeth determine strip width and how easily the tool clogs. Look for hardened stainless steel that stays sharp and resists rust. The Vibrant Kitchen uses 420J2 stainless steel, and the Sunkuka uses 18/8 stainless. A serrated edge works better on firm vegetables than on soft ones. Dull teeth tear instead of slice, so a blade that dulls early will undo the whole point of the tool.

Toothed blades are awkward to handle loose. The OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler includes a clear flip-top safety cover, and most others list none. If the tool lives in a shared drawer, a cover is worth looking for. Without one, store it on a hook. Even with a cover, never run a thumb along the teeth to check sharpness.

Julienne cutting takes repeated firm strokes, so a soft or wide handle matters. The OXO models use soft non-slip grips, and the Deepfeel and Sunkuka use wide Y handles. The Vibrant Kitchen lists a 5.6-inch handle. Metal handles feel solid but give less cushioning. If your hands tire quickly, favor the OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler for its soft cushioning.

Food fibers lodge in julienne teeth and can be hard to rinse out. The Sunkuka ships with a cleaning brush, and the OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler is dishwasher safe. Open-frame designs rinse faster. Plan to clean immediately after use. Skipping this step is the most common reason julienne tools end up forgotten in a drawer.

Carrots, zucchini and cucumbers cut cleanly, while soft tomatoes and ripe produce can mash. The Vibrant Kitchen adds a cabbage shredding side for slaw. Match the tool to your usual produce. Firm vegetables are the safest bet for all six. Cut a long carrot into shorter lengths first for steadier strokes with any of these tools.

howWeEvaluated.title: Julienne capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each listing describes its strip-cutting blade and what produce it names. The OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler and OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler describe precise strips, and the Vibrant Kitchen adds cabbage shredding. Clear, specific descriptions earned more credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Peeling versatility
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each tool also peels. The Deiss PRO, Vibrant Kitchen, Sunkuka and Deepfeel combine peeling with julienne, while the OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler is strips only. Tools that do both jobs earn flexibility credit, but we did not assume the julienne side matches a dedicated blade.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handle and comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed handle size and material. The OXO models use soft non-slip grips, the Sunkuka is all metal, and the Deepfeel uses a wide Y handle. Listings that give a handle length, like the 5.6 inches on the Vibrant Kitchen, were easier to judge than ones that only say ergonomic.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and cleaning
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted safety covers, brushes and dishwasher claims. The OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler has a cover and the Sunkuka has a brush. Teeth that clog easily lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered warranty and extras, such as the Deiss PRO lifetime warranty. We relied on product specs and buyer feedback, not hands-on measurement.

faq.q: What is a julienne peeler used for?
faq.a: It cuts thin matchstick strips from firm vegetables such as carrots, zucchini and cucumbers. You draw it along the vegetable like a peeler. The result suits salads, slaw, stir-fries and garnishes. It replaces a mandoline for small jobs. For best results, use firm, dry produce and long steady strokes.

faq.q: Can a julienne peeler also peel?
faq.a: Some can. The Deiss PRO, Vibrant Kitchen, Sunkuka and Deepfeel combine a peeling edge with julienne teeth, while the OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler is strips only. Combos save space but compromise slightly on each function. A dedicated tool stays focused.

Firm vegetables such as carrots, zucchini, cucumbers and potatoes cut cleanest. Soft ripe produce can mash against the teeth. The Vibrant Kitchen also lists cabbage for slaw. Chill vegetables briefly if they feel soft.

faq.q: How do I clean the teeth?
faq.a: Rinse right after use so fibers do not dry on. The Sunkuka includes a cleaning brush, and the OXO Good Grips Julienne Prep Peeler is dishwasher safe. Open-frame designs rinse quickly. Dry the tool before storing. A soft brush works well on any of these if yours does not include one.

They are safe with sensible handling, but the teeth are sharp. The OXO Good Grips Julienne Peeler includes a clear flip-top cover. Keep fingers clear of the blade and store covered or on a hook. Pull away from your body. Choose a tool with a cover if kids or guests share your kitchen.

faq.q: Do I need a dedicated julienne peeler if I own a mandoline?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but a peeler is faster for small jobs and has far less to wash. It also has no big blade to set up. For large batches, a mandoline may still be quicker. Think about how often you will really use it before buying more equipment.

faq.q: How long does the blade last?
faq.a: It depends on use and steel quality. Hardened stainless options such as the Vibrant Kitchen 420J2 are meant to stay keen. If strips start tearing or the tool needs extra pressure, replace it. Gentle hand washing helps the teeth last longer than a heavy dishwasher cycle.
